coordinate_system: Game Y-up at level.rotate_z_degrees=180; vector points towards sun, opposite ground shadow. No geographic north assumed.
method: Delft direction fitted offline from source-ground brightness versus full-scene voxel visibility; other levels use manual visual estimates from source-camera, overhead and height-sliced renders. Elevation, radiance and color are approximate artistic fits, not recovered capture metadata.

nmbu-park-03.evidence: Long lamp and tree shadows run mainly towards +X and slightly -Z across the path and lawn. The isolated lamp shadow in the lower overhead view is useful. Sun is opposite, towards -X/+Z; long shadows suggest a relatively low sun.

madras-square.evidence: Repeated cone and freestanding barrier shadows extend towards -X/+Z. The triangular barrier and paired signs provide independent checks. Short cone shadows suggest higher sun than NMBU. This level has no driving collision yet.

saburi-alley-yazd.evidence: The corner at the junction casts a broad shadow mainly towards -X across the lane; the opposite facade is illuminated in the source view. +X dominates; the small Z component is uncertain because the junction shadow is partly hidden.

basilica-assumption.evidence: Warm low-angle light on upper towers, lower facade and much of courtyard in shade. A bright strip at the +X/+Z side supports light from that side, but no isolated complete caster/shadow pair is visible. Azimuth and elevation remain provisional; use a weaker, wider highlight.

trompetstraat-delft.confidence: medium; fitted to baked road brightness and source voxel visibility
trompetstraat-delft.evidence: Fitted from 2,510 source-ground median log-luminance samples and full-scene 20 cm voxel visibility. Best candidate azimuth 168 degrees, elevation 32 degrees (game +Z azimuth reference); correlation 0.550. The old +X-dominant direction predicted the entire sampled road in shade. Updated direction points mostly -Z with a smaller +X component; ground shadows extend mostly +Z and slightly -X. Capture materials and indirect lighting limit precision.
